package_info.why_malicious: These versions of Apache Tomcat contain a vulnerability (CVE-2019-0232) that allows remote code execution due to improper input sanitization and unsafe command construction in the CGI Servlet, especially on Windows systems. Attackers can exploit this to execute arbitrary system commands.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Constructs a command line argument string for process execution using unsanitized user input (the 'command' variable). If the command contains spaces, it is wrapped in quotes.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Directly incorporates user-controlled input into a command string without sanitization, enabling command injection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would sanitize or strictly validate user input before using it in process execution. Here, user input is used verbatim.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate CGI implementations may construct command lines, but should always sanitize input.
key_indicators: User input used in process execution
Lack of input validation or sanitization
Command string construction with user data

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted HTTP request to the Tomcat CGI Servlet, supplying malicious input in the 'command' parameter.
attack_chain.leads_to: Unsanitized input is incorporated into the command line.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable code constructs a command string using the supplied input and executes it on the Windows system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary command execution on the server.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains remote code execution, potentially compromising the entire system.

behavioral_signatures: CGI Servlet invocation with unusual or suspicious command parameters
Process execution initiated by Tomcat with arguments derived from HTTP requests
Unexpected child processes spawned by Tomcat on Windows
file_indicators: Presence of vulnerable versions of org.apache.tomcat:tomcat-catalina or org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core
Configuration files enabling CGI Servlet with 'enableCmdLineArguments' set to true
network_indicators: Unusual outbound connections initiated by Tomcat processes
HTTP requests to Tomcat endpoints with suspicious command parameters
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for process execution events where Tomcat is the parent process and the command line includes arguments derived from HTTP requests. Audit Tomcat configuration for CGI Servlet usage and the 'enableCmdLineArguments' setting. Use vulnerability scanners to detect affected Tomcat versions. Look for suspicious HTTP requests targeting CGI endpoints with command injection patterns.
